objects.description: A simple fixed-point low-pass filter class. Maintains internal fixed-point accumulator (SmoothDataFP) and integer output (SmoothDataINT). Parameters Beta (shift-based smoothing factor, 2^Beta window) and FP_Shift (fractional bits) control filtering. Methods: update applies the filter to a new sample, init seeds internal state from the first input, reset marks state to be reinitialized on next update, value returns last integer output. ICACHE_RAM_ATTR suggests placement in fast instruction RAM on some embedded platforms (e.g., ESP8266/ESP32). Construction: default Beta=3, FP_Shift=5; overloaded constructors allow setting Beta and optionally FP_Shift. Destruction: trivial; no dynamic resources. Usage: call update with int32 samples; call reset before first use or between sequences to re-seed on next update.

functions.name: LPF::update
functions.description: Updates the fixed-point low-pass filter with a new input sample and returns the current smoothed value as a 32-bit integer. On the first call after construction or reset, it seeds the filter state with Indata via init() and returns that value. Subsequent calls apply a simple IIR low-pass using internal parameters Beta (filter length exponent) and FP_Shift (fractional bits). Intended for fast, integer-only smoothing on embedded targets.
requirements: This is a non-static member function; the LPF instance must be constructed before calling.
Indata must be representable as int32_t.
To avoid signed 32-bit overflow, Indata << FP_Shift and intermediate computations should remain within int32_t range (caller should choose input magnitudes/Beta/FP_Shift accordingly).
No explicit thread-safety; do not call concurrently from multiple threads/ISRs unless externally synchronized.

functions.name: LPF::reset
functions.description: Marks the filter to be reinitialized on the next update() call. It does not change the returned value immediately; rather, the next update(Indata) will call init(Indata) internally and re-seed the filter.
requirements: This is a non-static member function; the LPF instance must be constructed before calling.
After reset(), call update() (or init()) before relying on value().

functions.name: LPF::init
functions.description: Initializes (seeds) the filter state with the provided input value. Sets both the integer and fixed-point internal states based on Indata and FP_Shift, and clears the reset flag. Useful for explicitly seeding before the first update().
requirements: This is a non-static member function; the LPF instance must be constructed before calling.
Indata must be representable as int32_t.
To avoid signed 32-bit overflow, (Indata << FP_Shift) should fit within int32_t.

functions.name: LPF::value
functions.description: Returns the current smoothed value as a 32-bit integer. This reflects the last update/init state.
requirements: Call init() or update() at least once before calling value(); otherwise the returned value may be uninitialized/undefined.
This is a const, non-static member function; the LPF instance must be constructed and remain alive during the call.

functions.name: deferExecutionMicros
functions.signature: void deferExecutionMicros(unsigned long us, std::function<void()> f)
functions.description: Schedules a function object f to be executed after a delay specified in microseconds. Implementation details are not shown; typical use is to defer work to occur at/after a target time on embedded platforms.
requirements: us is an unsigned long delay in microseconds; valid range is whatever fits in unsigned long for the platform.
f must be a valid callable object; it should remain valid until execution and be safe to invoke without parameters.
Behavior on exceptions thrown by f is unknown (not documented).
Exact timing source and scheduling semantics are unknown (not documented).

functions.name: executeDeferredFunction
functions.description: Processes and executes a previously deferred function when its scheduled time has arrived, using the provided current time value. Exact scheduling semantics are not shown.
requirements: now is the current time in microseconds as an unsigned long, using the same timebase as used by deferExecutionMicros (inferred from naming).
Call this in the context where deferred functions should run (e.g., main loop/ISR) according to your platform; exact calling requirements are not documented.

functions.name: deferExecutionMillis
functions.signature: static inline void deferExecutionMillis(unsigned long ms, std::function<void()> f)
functions.description: Convenience wrapper that defers execution in milliseconds by calling deferExecutionMicros(ms * 1000, f). Use when specifying delays in milliseconds instead of microseconds.
requirements: ms is an unsigned long delay in milliseconds; ms * 1000 must fit in unsigned long to avoid overflow before conversion to microseconds.
f must be a valid callable object suitable for deferExecutionMicros.
Relies on deferExecutionMicros being available and correctly implemented.
